title: Not Being Lazy
note: He defines this as not slacking when you do what you have planned. Even those with drive can at times grow lazy through the pull of their nature, so this follows the chapter on drive.

couplets.plain: The unfailing lamp called family goes out and is lost when the grime called laziness creeps over it.
couplets.pm: The unfailing lamp of the family you were born into dies when the darkness of your laziness presses on it. A family lights up those born in it for as long as the world goes on. Laziness comes from the dull quality in us, and unlike other darkness it can smother the lamp itself. “Lost” means not even the name is left.

links.reason: Laziness is the grime that puts out a family’s unfailing lamp.

couplets.plain: Those who want their family to be a true family should treat laziness as the laziness it is.
couplets.pm: Those who want the family they were born in to grow ever better should regard laziness as laziness and live by effort. Nothing is worse than it, as nothing is crueller than fire, so he calls it only by its own name. If they strive they rise, and the family rises. If not, it falls. Some read மடியா as “destroying it”.

links.quote: treat laziness as the laziness it is
links.reason: Tells those who want a true family to treat laziness as what it is.

links.quote: want their family to be a true family
links.reason: Takes making a family truly a family as the goal worth shunning laziness for.

couplets.plain: The family of a fool who carries laziness within will perish before the fool does.
couplets.pm: The family of the ignorant man who carries within him the laziness he ought to drop perishes even before he does. He is a fool because he keeps inside him what destroys him. The family goes first because he is the one who sustains it. It rises after him but falls before him.

links.reason: Says the fool who carries laziness within sees the family die first, in the fool’s own lifetime.

couplets.plain: For those who fall into laziness and make no fine effort, the family dies and faults multiply.
couplets.pm: Those who have fallen into laziness have no refined effort. Their family perishes and their faults multiply. He names those faults later.

links.quote: the family dies and faults multiply

couplets.plain: Delay, forgetfulness, laziness and sleep: these four are the boat that those bound for ruin desire.
couplets.pm: Laziness, dragging out what should be done quickly, forgetting and sleep are the ship that people whose days are ending gladly board. They look like pleasure to those bound for suffering, then drop them in it, as a ship seems to promise gain, then drops them in the sea. Some read கலன் as a jewel worn with desire.

links.quote: the boat that those bound for ruin desire
links.reason: These habits are a boat that people board gladly, and it carries them to ruin.
Names delay first among the four that carry people to ruin.

couplets.plain: Even when they hold all that the lords of the earth hold, the lazy won’t easily win any great good.
couplets.pm: Even when wealth like that of those who rule the whole earth comes to them unsought, the lazy get no great joy from it. They make no effort to guard that wealth, so it goes, and their suffering stays. Some read this as “even when rulers of the whole earth become their allies”.
couplets.note: The Tamil can also mean the support of the earth’s rulers. He mentions that reading and takes பற்று as wealth.

links.quote: the lazy won’t easily win any great good
links.reason: Even with all that the lords of the earth hold, the lazy can’t win any great good.

couplets.plain: Those who love laziness and make no fine effort will hear words of rebuke and scorn.
couplets.pm: Those who love laziness and so have no fine effort will hear their friends reproach them again and again before their own people, and then, when that does no good, speak of them with scorn. If friends scorn them, others surely will. They have no power to answer any of it, so they can only hear it.

links.quote: will hear words of rebuke and scorn

couplets.plain: If laziness settles in someone of good family, it will make them a slave to their enemies.
couplets.pm: Laziness means neglecting the work. If it settles in a ruler who ought to be raising his family, it brings him to be a slave of his enemies, bowing low and taking their orders.

links.quote: make them a slave to their enemies
links.reason: Laziness settling in someone of good family ends in slavery to their enemies.

couplets.plain: When a man ends the rule of laziness over him, the faults that have entered his family and his manhood are gone.
couplets.pm: When a man gets rid of his habit of being ruled by laziness, which comes from the dull quality in him, the faults in his family and his manhood go. These are faults that arose earlier from other causes, not from laziness. They too leave once he drops it and takes up effort.

links.quote: ends the rule of laziness over him
links.reason: Shows how much laziness was costing: end it and the faults in family and manhood go.

couplets.plain: A ruler free of laziness will gain, all at once, everything the one who measured with his feet strode over.
couplets.pm: A ruler without laziness gains, all at once and not by stages, the whole expanse crossed by the god who measured every world with his foot. He is always striving at his work, so he gains it without a break.

links.quote: everything the one who measured with his feet strode over
links.reason: Freedom from laziness alone would win a ruler all that was crossed by the one who measured with his feet.

ideaLinks.quote: The unfailing lamp called family goes out
ideaLinks.reason: Laziness puts out the family’s lamp, brings it down and leaves it in ruin.
